title: Biomembrane Fabrication by the Solvent-assisted Lipid Bilayer (SALB) Method
protocol: Prepare lipid stock solutions of 10 mg/ml DOPC and 1 mg/ml Rh-PE by dissolving lipids in isopropanol.
Dilute and mix stock solutions to prepare desired lipid mixture for fluorescence microscopy and FRAP experiments, including 0.5 wt% Rh-PE.
Inject the lipid mixture into the microfluidic channel until filled.
Incubate the lipid mixture on the glass surface for about 10 minutes.
Gradually replace the lipid solution with water or buffer using a peristaltic pump at a low flow rate of 10-50 µl/min.
Alternatively, replace the lipid mixture by repeated pipetting to rinse thoroughly with excess buffer to remove residual isopropanol.
Prepare a stock solution containing 10 mg/ml DOPC lipid, 10 mg/ml cholesterol, and 1 mg/ml Rh-PE by dissolving powders in isopropanol.
Repeat steps 1.2-1.6 using the stock solutions prepared.
Immerse the glass slide in a 1% sodium dodecyl sulfate (SDS) solution for 10 min.
Wash the slides thoroughly with deionized water.
Rinse the slides with ethanol.
Blow-dry the slides using a gentle stream of nitrogen.
Expose the slides to oxygen plasma for 30 sec at maximum radiofrequency power in the oxygen plasma chamber.
Remove the protective film coating of the bottomless commercial microfluidic chamber using tweezers.
Attach the glass slide onto the sticky side of the chamber.
Assemble the connectors and tubing into the inlet and outlet positions of the chamber.
Place the microfluidic channel on the microscope stage.
Form a fluorescently-labeled supported lipid bilayer in the microfluidic channel using the desired lipid composition (e.g., 0.5 mg/ml DOPC) including 0.5 wt% Rh-PE in organic solvent.
Locate the bilayer plane with a 60X oil immersion objective (NA 1.49).
Take two pre-bleach images before photobleaching.
Photo-bleach a 30 µm wide circular spot with a 532 nm, 100 mW laser beam after warming up the laser until its intensity has become stable.
Immediately after photobleaching, capture a series of images every 1 sec for 2 min to follow the recovery in fluorescence intensity at the bleached spot.
Expose the silicon dioxide-coated quartz crystal sensor chip to oxygen plasma for 30 seconds at maximum radiofrequency power in the oxygen plasma chamber.
Remove the chip from the chamber and immediately mount it in the measurement chamber.
Acquire the frequency and dissipation of the sensor chip in air before starting the experiment.
Run the Q-Soft software program and click “Acquisition” then select “Setup Measurement.”
Check overtones 3, 5, 7, 9, 11, and 13 in the new window that appears.
Click Find and Run to check the resonance spectra.
Set the temperature at 24 °C.
If one or more resonance frequencies do not agree with expected values, re-perform chip mounting checks until agreement is reached.
Start the peristaltic pump and flow buffer solution (10 mM Tris, 150 mM NaCl, pH 7.5) into the measurement chamber at a rate of 100 µl/min.
Click “Acquisition” then select “Restart Measurement” to record resonance frequency and energy dissipation signals.
Repeat this step until a stable baseline is obtained for frequency and dissipation shifts.
Inject isopropanol (without lipid) for 10 minutes.
Inject the mixture of DOPC lipid/cholesterol at the desired molar ratio with a total lipid concentration of 0.5 mg/ml in isopropanol for 10 min.
Inject buffer for 20 min at a flow rate of 100 µl/min.
Inject a solution of 1 mM methyl-β-cyclodextrin (MβCD) prepared in buffer (flow rate 100 µl/min) until the frequency signal reaches a stable value.
Measure the relative positive frequency shifts caused by the MβCD treatment step.
Calculate the mass of cholesterol and DOPC lipids by converting the Δfcho and ΔfDOPC values to mass values using the Sauerbrey equation [Δm = -(C/n)×Δf, where C=17.7 ng/cm2, n:overtone].
Calculate the mole fraction of cholesterol in the SLB, taking into account the molecular weights of DOPC lipid (786.1 g/mol) and cholesterol (386.6 g/mol).
